methodological_rigor.justification: The study triangulates findings across multiple orthogonal approaches — public human scRNA-seq (GSE182109), murine scRNA-seq (GSE236243), flow cytometry across four tumor models (CT2A, E0771, Yummer1.7, cLCMV), bulk RNA-seq of sorted TIM3+ CD8+ T cells (n=6/arm), TNFR2-KO mice, and pharmacologic antagonism combined with anti–PD-1. T-cell intrinsic effects are rigorously isolated via a 1:1 WT CD45.1 / KO CD45.2 Trp2-TCR-tg adoptive transfer into the same recipient (Fig. 4D). CD8 depletion establishes mechanism and the rechallenge experiment (6–9 months) credibly interrogates memory. Statistical methods are appropriate: paired/unpaired t-tests, two-way repeated-measures ANOVA, linear regression with R² reporting, Kaplan–Meier log-rank, and explicit Bonferroni-style α correction for multiple survival comparisons (α=0.05/6=0.00833). Limitations: no a priori power calculation is reported, randomization and blinding of outcome assessment are not described, PMA/ionomycin stimulation findings are only partially corroborated by gp33 (granzyme B result diverges — Supplementary Fig. S5A), and in vitro cytotoxicity relies on 5 biological replicates with only ex vivo ConA/IL2-activated splenocytes.

clinical_relevance_loe.justification: This is a preclinical mechanistic study using murine syngeneic tumor models, KO mice, in vitro assays, and public human scRNA-seq — Oxford LoE 5. Clinical/translational relevance is nonetheless high: TNFR2 is identified as an upstream regulator of TOX, a central transcription factor of terminal exhaustion, and the authors demonstrate that pharmacologic TNFR2 antagonism combined with anti–PD-1 produces 50–60% long-term survival in subcutaneous and intracranial GBM models with durable memory on rechallenge. GBM is a notoriously ICI-refractory disease, so a combinatorial strategy that works intracranially is a plausible near-term translational lead. A commercial antagonist (BE0247) already exists and TNFR2-targeted therapeutics are in early clinical development, strengthening the translational path, though human efficacy and off-target toxicity (TNFR2 on Tregs, endothelium) remain unaddressed.

reporting_quality.justification: ARRIVE applies as the dominant content is animal experimentation with cell lines. Reporting is thorough for animal husbandry, IACUC approval (A163-21-08), sex/age matching rationale (male-only for Yummer1.7 due to female tumor rejection), humane endpoints, antibody RRIDs, and cell line provenance/mycoplasma status. Bulk RNA-seq raw data are deposited (GEO GSE297330) and public datasets (GSE160189, GSE182109, GSE236243) are reused with citations. Custom R scripts are indicated as available (locations redacted in blinded version). Gaps against ARRIVE: no explicit randomization or allocation concealment, no blinding of outcome assessment stated, no a priori sample-size justification, and attrition/exclusions (e.g., censoring rules for ulceration) are described only for tumor-volume endpoints.

novelty_literature.justification: The core conceptual claim — TNFR2 acts upstream of TOX during the Tex_prog → Tex_term transition and loss of TNFR2 uncouples TIM3 from TOX, yielding a novel PD-1+TIM3+TOX^lo population with hybrid progenitor/terminal features — is a genuine mechanistic advance. Prior work on TNFR2 in cancer (refs. 34, 35) and on TNF in exhaustion (ref. 30) establishes the broader context, and NFAT/AP1 and TOX pathways (refs. 25–28) are well mapped; this study specifically fills the gap of what sits upstream of TOX induction. The combination of TNFR2 antagonism with anti–PD-1 in an intracranial GBM model with durable memory on rechallenge is also novel and clinically meaningful. Novelty is tempered by overlap with the authors' own recent prior work on TAM-driven exhaustion (ref. 24) and the fact that TNFR2 as a cancer immunotherapy target is already an active field.

writing_presentation.justification: The manuscript is well-organized with clear progression from scRNA-seq discovery, through phenotypic/functional validation, to KO and pharmacologic intervention. The abstract is self-contained and accurately previews findings. Figure captions are detailed, standalone-interpretable, and include statistical tests, sample sizes, and dosing (e.g., Fig. 6 legend lists corrected p-value threshold 0.0083 and n=20/group). Minor issues include occasional typos ('lymphocyet', 'Nfact3' vs 'Nfatc3'), a few long sentences in the Discussion that chain multiple mechanistic claims, and some redundancy between Introduction and Discussion on TNFR2 biology. Overall clarity and precision are appropriate for a specialist immunology audience.

key_strengths: Mechanistic advance positioning TNFR2 upstream of TOX, with a defined novel PD-1+TIM3+TOX^lo exhausted population and corroborating bulk RNA-seq showing downregulated NFAT/exhaustion programs and upregulated AP1 signatures
Multi-model validation across subcutaneous and intracranial GBM, breast, melanoma, and cLCMV, with public human GBM scRNA-seq triangulation
Rigorous T-cell intrinsic design using co-transferred WT (CD45.1) and TNFR2-KO (CD45.2) Trp2-TCR-tg cells into the same recipient
Translational payoff: anti-TNFR2 + anti–PD-1 yields 50–60% long-term survival with durable memory on rechallenge in an ICI-refractory intracranial GBM model
Appropriate statistical correction for multiplicity in survival comparisons (α=0.05/6) and multiple analytical outputs (tumor volume, time-to-endpoint, normalized AUC burden)
key_concerns: No a priori power calculation, randomization procedure, or blinded outcome assessment reported — ARRIVE items incompletely addressed
Divergent findings between PMA/ionomycin and physiologic gp33 restimulation (granzyme B increase not reproduced; Supplementary Fig. S5A) deserve more explicit reconciliation
Mechanism linking TNFR2 → NFAT → TOX remains correlative; direct biochemical/epigenetic evidence (e.g., ATAC-seq, NFAT nuclear translocation in TNFR2-KO) is not provided
Off-target effects of systemic TNFR2 antagonism on Tregs, endothelium, NK, and glial cells are acknowledged but not experimentally dissected
No tumor control benefit in Yummer1.7 is reported but not mechanistically explained, raising questions about generalizability
Code availability is referenced but redacted; ARRIVE-level documentation of inclusion/exclusion and ulceration censoring is partial
chief_reviewer.rationale: A methodologically strong, multi-model preclinical immunology study with a credible mechanistic claim (TNFR2 upstream of TOX) and a translationally meaningful combinatorial efficacy signal in intracranial GBM, placing it comfortably within Tier 2 (Cancer Research / Clinical Cancer Research / Nature Communications range); it falls short of Tier 1 due to correlative mechanistic linkage, incomplete ARRIVE reporting, and lack of human efficacy data.
